Rashi on Yevamot 20a:14:1.hebrew: אלה המצות - בסוף ספר תורת כהנים, ומשמע דאכול' ספרא קאי, וכל אזהרת כהנים התם כתיבא:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:14:1.english: These are the mitzvot - [This is written] at the end of the book of Torat Kohanim [Leviticus], and it implies that it refers to the entire book, and every prohibition regarding priests is written there.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:15:1.english: Sanctify yourself - To hold back and be careful.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:15:2.hebrew: אף במותר לך - להוסיף עליהם שניות, המותר לך על העריות, כדי שלא תבא לידי עריות האסורות מן התורה:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:15:2.english: Even in that which is permitted to you - to add to them secondary [forbidden relationships] — that which is permitted to you beyond the [biblically] forbidden relationships — so that you do not come to [transgress] forbidden relationships that are prohibited by the Torah.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:16:1.hebrew: קפסיק ותני - אלמנה לכ"ג, לא שנא נפלה לפניו מן הנשואין, דהיינו תרתי לגריעותא: חדא, דאלמנה היא ואיכא לאו ד"אלמנה לא יקח", ועוד, דבעולה היא ואיכא איסור עשה לגביה, דכתיב "אשה בבתוליה יקח" — ולא בעולה — ולאו הבא מכלל עשה, עשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:16:1.english: [The Tanna] states categorically - [regarding] a widow to a High Priest, it makes no difference whether she fell before him [for levirate marriage] from marriage, which involves two disqualifications: first, that she is a widow, and there is the negative commandment of "A widow ... he shall not take"; and furthermore, that she is a non-virgin, and there is a prohibition of a positive commandment regarding him, as it is written, "He shall take a wife in her virginity" — and not a non-virgin — and a negative commandment inferred from a positive commandment [has the status of] a positive commandment.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:16:2.hebrew: ולא שנא - נפלה לפניו מן האירוסין ועודה בתולה, דליכא אלא לאו דאלמנה:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:16:2.english: And it is no different - [if] she fell before him [for levirate marriage] from betrothal while she is still a virgin, where there is only the negative commandment of a widow.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:17:1.english: Let the positive commandment come - [That is, the commandment] of "her brother-in-law shall cohabit with her" [Deuteronomy 25:5].

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:18:1.hebrew: ועלתה השערה מצי למכתב - דהא כתיב ברישא דקרא "לקחת את יבמתו", מה ת"ל "יבמתו":
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:18:1.english: [The verse] could have written: “And she shall ascend to the gate” - For it is written in the beginning of the verse: “to take his yevama”; why, [then,] does the verse state “his yevama”?

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:18:2.hebrew: יש לך יבמה כו' - דאם כתב "ולא יחפוץ האיש לקחת את יבמתו ועלתה השערה", הוה משמע דההיא דקרינא ביה "לקחת" הוא דקא מצרכה רחמנא "ועלתה השערה" לחלוץ, אבל חייבי לאוין, דלא קרינן בהו "לקחת", לא קרינן בה "ועלתה". להכי הדר כתב "יבמתו", למימר דיש לך יבמה אחרת שעולה השערה לחלוץ, ואע"ג דלא כתיב בה "לקחת", שאין עולה לייבום:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:18:2.english: There is one yevama, etc. - For if [Scripture] had written, "And if the man does not wish to take his yevama, then she shall ascend to the gate," it would have implied that [it is] the one to whom we apply "to take" whom the Merciful One requires [to fulfill] "then she shall ascend to the gate" to perform ḥalitza; however, [regarding] those liable for [violating] negative commandments, to whom we do not apply "to take," we would not apply to her "then she shall ascend." Therefore, [Scripture] went back and wrote "his yevama," to state that there is another yevama who ascends to the gate to perform ḥalitza, even though "to take" is not written regarding her, since she does not ascend for levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:19:1.hebrew: אימא חייבי כריתות - נמי לילף מהכא דליבעי חליצה, ואמאי פטרינן לגמרי:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:19:1.english: Say [that] those liable to karet - let us also derive from here that they require chalitzah, and why do we exempt [them] completely?

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:1:1.hebrew: שמגרשה בגט - ואינה צריכה חליצה, ואם רצה להחזיר מחזירה, ולא אמרינן מצוה רמיא רחמנא עליה ועבדה, ומהשתא תיקו עליה באיסור אשת אח:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:1:1.english: That he divorces her with a bill of divorce - And she does not require chalitzah, and if he wishes to take [her] back, he may take her back; and we do not say [that] the Merciful One imposed a mitzvah upon him and he performed it, and from now on she stands [forbidden] to him under the prohibition of a brother's wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:1:2.english: Let us say - [that] the first levirate bond is still upon her, and she should require ḥalitza.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:3:1.english: Toss that which is permitted - To expound [the phrase] "and he shall take her" [to teach] that she does not require ḥalitza.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:3:2.hebrew: אהיתרא - היכא דכולה מילתא היתר, כגון במייבם אשת אח:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:3:2.english: On that which is permitted - Where the entire matter is permitted, such as in [the case of] one who performs levirate marriage with a brother's wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:3:3.hebrew: ושדי איסורא - למדרש "ויבמה", עדיין יבומין עליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:3:3.english: And toss that which is prohibited - [That is,] to expound [the word] "and he shall perform levirate marriage with her" [as teaching that] the levirate obligation is still upon her.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:3:4.english: On that which is prohibited - [That is,] where there is an aspect of prohibition, such as with the wife of his brother who was not in his world [i.e., with whom he did not coexist].

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:4:1.hebrew: אחותו מאמו שנשאה אחיו מאביו - קודם לידתו של זה, וכשנולד זה מצאה נשואה לאחיו — תתייבם לו כשימות זה, דהא מצאה בהיתר ייבום:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:4:1.english: His maternal sister whom his paternal brother married - before this [brother's] birth, and when this [brother] was born, he found her married to his brother — she should enter into levirate marriage with him when this [married brother] dies, since he found her in a state permitted [for] levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:5:1.hebrew: איסור אחותו לית ליה היתר - אבל איסור אשת אח אית ליה היתר כשאין לו בנים. הילכך, כשמת ראשון בלא בנים, פקע איסורו לגבי שני ונשאה, והשלישי מכח שני בא:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:5:1.english: The prohibition [against marrying] his sister has no dispensation - However, the prohibition [against marrying] a brother's wife has a dispensation when he has no children. Therefore, when the first [brother] died without children, its prohibition ceased with respect to the second [brother] and he married her, and the third [brother] comes by virtue of the second.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:6:1.hebrew: לא חולצת ולא מתייבמת - צרתה, וכ"ש היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:6:1.english: Neither performs ḥalitza nor enters into levirate marriage - [This refers to] her rival wife, and all the more so she herself.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:6:2.english: A prohibition of a mitzva - [The Mishnah] proceeds to explain them.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:6:3.english: The expression 'mitzva' and 'sanctity' is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:7:1.hebrew: אחותה - של ערוה כשהיא יבמתה, כגון שנפלו שתי אחיות משני אחין, האחת אסורה משום ערוה, כגון שהיא כלתו או חמותו:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:7:1.english: Her sister - [the sister] of the forbidden relation, when she is her yevama, such as when two sisters fell [before him for levirate marriage] from two brothers, [and] one [of them] is forbidden [to him] because of a forbidden relation, such as when she is his daughter-in-law or his mother-in-law.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:7:2.hebrew: או חולצת או מתייבמת - אחות הערוה, דלא פגע באחות זקוקתו, משום דערוה לאו זקוקתו היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:7:2.english: Either performs ḥalitza or enters into levirate marriage - [This refers to] the sister of the forbidden relation, for he does not encounter the sister of [a woman] bound to him [by a levirate bond], because a forbidden relation is not bound to him.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:8:1.hebrew: שניות - שניות לעריות שגזרו סופרים עליהם, ובגמ' מפרש לה:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:8:1.english: Secondary - Secondary [degrees of] forbidden relationships that the Sages decreed upon them, and in the Gemara [it] explains it.

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:8:2.hebrew: אלמנה לכ"ג - שמת אחיו ההדיוט ונפלה אלמנתו לפניו:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:8:2.english: A widow to a High Priest - Where his brother, a common [priest], died and his widow fell before him [for levirate marriage].

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:8:3.hebrew: גרושה וחלוצה לכהן הדיוט - שעבר אחיו המת ונשא חלוצה וגרושה, וכשמת צריכה חליצה, שהרי תופסים לו בה קידושין, דקידושין תופסים בחייבי לאוין. אבל יבומי לא, שהרי אסורה לו לזה שהוא כהן, ואפטורי בולא כלום לא, דלא אלים לאו למיפטרה, דילפי' מאחות אשה בפ"ק (דף ג:):
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:8:3.english: A divorcée or a chalutzah to a common priest - [This refers to a case] where his deceased brother transgressed and married a chalutzah or a divorcée, and when he died, she requires chalitzah, for betrothal takes effect for him with her, since betrothal takes effect with [women forbidden by] negative commandments. However, levirate marriage [may] not [be performed], for she is forbidden to this [surviving brother] who is a priest; and to be exempted with nothing at all [is] not [possible], because a negative commandment is not strong [enough] to exempt her, as we derive from [the case of] a wife's sister in the first chapter (3b).

Rashi on Yevamot 20a:9:1.hebrew: לאיתויי צרת אילונית כרב אסי - בפ"ק (דף יב.) דלא חולצת ולא מתייבמת, דערוה קרינן בה באילונית, דמיעטה קרא מאשר תלד, וקיימא עליה באיסור אשת אח. הילכך, צרתה צרת ערוה:
Rashi on Yevamot 20a:9:1.english: To include the rival wife of an aylonit, like Rav Asi - In the first chapter (12a), [where he states] that she neither performs chalitzah nor enters into levirate marriage, for we call the aylonit a forbidden relation, since Scripture excluded her from "[whom] she will bear," and she remains [forbidden] to him under the prohibition of a brother's wife. Therefore, her rival wife is the rival wife of a forbidden relation.

Tosafot on Yevamot 20a:17:1.hebrew: בשלמא מן הנשואין כו' - תימה, דמן הנשואין נמי תיקשי ליה: דאמאי חולצת, כיון דאין עולה לייבום דלא אתי עשה ודחי לא תעשה ועשה, ותיהוי כי חייבי כריתות? וי"ל, דלא קאמר "בשלמא" אלא ממאי דאין מתייבמת:
Tosafot on Yevamot 20a:17:1.english: Granted, [if she is a widow] from marriage, etc. - This is surprising, for [in the case of a widow] from marriage as well, it should be difficult [for the Gemara]: why does she perform chalitzah, since she is not eligible for levirate marriage because a positive commandment does not come and override both a prohibition and a positive commandment — so let her be like those [forbidden] under penalty of karet [who require neither chalitzah nor levirate marriage]? And one can answer that [the Gemara] only said "Granted" with respect to the fact that she does not enter into levirate marriage.

Tosafot on Yevamot 20a:17:2.hebrew: יבא עשה וידחה לא תעשה - הקשה ריב"א בפ"ב דסנהדרין (דף יט. ושם): דכיון דאין אשה מתעברת מביאה ראשונה, כדאמר בסוף פ' ד' אחין (לקמן יבמות ד' לד. ושם), היאך תתיבם? דבביא' ראשונה ליכא הקמת שם, וביאה שניה אסירא ליה כדאמר לקמן: גזירה ביאה ראשונה אטו ביאה שניה. ואר"י דלא קשה מידי: דלא בעינן שתהא הביאה ראויה להקמת שם, אלא שהיבמה והיבם יהו ראוין להקמת שם; ולא ממעטינן אלא אילונית וסריס שאינן ראוין לילד לעולם, אבל ביאה שאין יכולה להתעבר בה לא ממעטי, כיון שהאשה או היבם ראוין לבסוף להוליד. דאל"כ, תיקשה היאך קטנה מתייבמת לרבנן? וגם לרבי מאיר היתה מתייבמת אי לאו חששא דשמא תמצא אילונית. ובפרק ב"ש (לקמן יבמות דף קיא:) תנן: "קטן הבא על הגדולה תגדלנו". ובפ' הבא על יבמתו (לקמן יבמות נה:) נמי מרבינן דנקנית בביאה שלא כדרכה והעראה, אע"פ שאין מתעברת בה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 20a:17:2.english: Let a positive mitzvah come and override a prohibition - Riva raised a difficulty in the second chapter of Sanhedrin (19a, and there): Since a woman does not conceive from the first act of intercourse, as [the Gemara] states at the end of the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achim (later, Yevamot 34a, and there), how can she enter into levirate marriage? For in the first act of intercourse there is no establishing of a name [i.e., potential for offspring], and the second act of intercourse is forbidden to him, as [the Gemara] states later: [the first act is prohibited as] a decree on account of the second act of intercourse. And R. Yitzchak says that there is no difficulty at all: For we do not require that [the act of intercourse itself] be fit for establishing a name, but rather that the yevamah and the yavam be fit for establishing a name; and we only exclude an ailonit [a congenitally sterile woman] and a saris [a sterile man] who are never fit to bear children, whereas an act of intercourse through which she cannot conceive is not excluded, since the woman or the yavam are ultimately fit to bear children. For if not so, it would be difficult: how can a minor girl enter into levirate marriage according to the Rabbis? And even according to Rabbi Meir, she would enter into levirate marriage were it not for the concern that she might turn out to be an ailonit. And in the chapter [entitled] Beit Shammai (later, Yevamot 111b), we learned in a Mishnah: "A minor boy who has intercourse with an adult woman — she raises him [as her husband]." And in the chapter [entitled] Haba Al Yevimto (later, Yevamot 55b) as well, we derive [from Scripture] that she is acquired through unnatural intercourse and initial contact (ha'ara'ah), even though she does not conceive through it.

Tosafot on Yevamot 20a:20:1.hebrew: אי הכי חייבי לאוין נמי - פי': כיון דאין עולים לייבום, לא יעלו לחליצה. ותימה לר"י: היכי מצי למימר דלא יעלו לחליצה? הא מיבמתו דשמעינן דאין עולין לייבום, מהתם שמעינן דעולין לחליצה, כדדרשינן: "יש לך יבמה אחרת שעולה לחליצה"! ועוד, דפריך "מה ראית" — פי': דאימא איפכא, ונוקי "יבמתו" לחייבי כרת ו"אם לא יחפוץ" לחייבי לאוין — היכי מצי למעוטי מאם לא יחפוץ חייבי לאוין מחליצה? הא קרינן בהו "אם חפץ יבם", דאתי עשה ודחי ל"ת, כיון דמוקמינן "יבמתו" לחייבי כריתות! וקצת היה נראה לפרש דה"פ: "א"ה חייבי לאוין נמי" — נשוה חליצה וייבום מהאי קרא. ותו פריך "מה ראית" — פירוש: דמהאי קרא "ולא יחפוץ" נשוה חייבי לאוין לחליצה וייבום, וליהוו בני חליצה וייבום. ואין להקשות דלמה לן קרא להכי, דלישתוק קרא מיני' — דטובא איצטריך, כדפרישית לקמן בפ' החולץ (יבמות דף מד.), ונייבם לחדא ונחלוץ לחדא. אבל קשה: דאם כן מאי קא משני "מיסתברא חייבי לאוין תפסי בהו קדושין", דמשמע מתוך התירוץ דהוא פריך שלא יעלו חייבי לאוין לחליצה? וי"ל בדוחק דמחייבי לאוין וחייבי עשה פריך, והכי פריך: "א"ה חייבי לאוין וחייבי עשה" — נשוה לחליצה וייבום מהאי קרא, וחייבי לאוין יעלו גם לייבום וחייבי עשה לא יעלו גם לחליצה; ועיקר פירכא מחייבי עשה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 20a:20:1.english: If so, [those] liable for a prohibition also [should not require ḥalitza] - Explanation: Since they are not eligible for levirate marriage, they should not be eligible for ḥalitza. And this is astonishing to R. Yitzchak: how could [the Gemara] say that they are not eligible for ḥalitza? Why, from [the word] “his yevama” — from which we learn that they are not eligible for levirate marriage — from that very [word] we learn that they are eligible for ḥalitza, as we expound: “You have another yevama who ascends for ḥalitza [but not for levirate marriage]”! Furthermore, when [the Gemara] asks, “And what did you see?” — meaning, say the opposite, and establish “his yevama” as referring to those liable to karet and “if he does not wish” as referring to those liable for a prohibition — how could one exclude those liable for a prohibition from ḥalitza based on “if he does not wish”? Why, we apply to them [the inference] “if he wishes, he performs levirate marriage,” since a positive commandment comes and overrides a negative prohibition, once we establish “his yevama” as referring to those liable to karet! It would somewhat appear [possible] to explain that this is its meaning: “If so, those liable for a prohibition also” — let us equate ḥalitza and levirate marriage from this verse. And then [the Gemara] asks, “And what did you see?” — meaning: from this verse “and he does not wish,” let us equate those liable for a prohibition with respect to ḥalitza and levirate marriage, so that they are subject to [both] ḥalitza and levirate marriage. And one should not raise the objection: why do we need a verse for this, let the verse omit it — for it is needed for much [else], as I explained below in the chapter HaCholetz (Yevamot 44a), that we should perform levirate marriage with one and ḥalitza with one. However, this is difficult: if so, what is [the Gemara] answering [when it says], “It stands to reason: betrothal takes effect with those liable for a prohibition,” from which answer it is implied that [the questioner] was asking that those liable for a prohibition should not be eligible for ḥalitza? One can answer with difficulty that [the Gemara] is asking from [both] those liable for a prohibition and those liable for a positive commandment, and this is what it is asking: “If so, those liable for a prohibition and those liable for a positive commandment” — let us equate [both] for ḥalitza and levirate marriage from this verse, so that those liable for a prohibition will also be eligible for levirate marriage, and those liable for a positive commandment will also not be eligible for ḥalitza; and the main objection is from those liable for a positive commandment.

Tosafot on Yevamot 20a:5:1.hebrew: האי איסורא דאית ליה התירא - דפקע איסור אשת אח, דיכול להחזירה לאחר שגרשה; וכי היכי דפקע ליה לגבי דידיה איסור אשת אח, פקע נמי לגבי אחיו הנולד, וה"ל אשת אחיו שהיה בעולמו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 20a:5:1.english: That prohibition has [a case where it is] permitted - For the prohibition of a brother's wife is abrogated, as he [the second brother] can remarry her after divorcing her; and just as the prohibition of a brother's wife is abrogated with respect to him, it is also abrogated with respect to his [newly] born brother, so she is [for him] the wife of his brother with whom he coexisted.

Tosafot on Yevamot 20a:9:1.hebrew: לאתויי צרת אילונית - אע"ג דמתני' לא קתני צרה, מ"מ הוי בכלל ד"כל שאיסורה איסור ערוה" — דמשמע שאיסורה בא מחמת ערוה, דהיינו הצרה. ולא הוצרך להזכיר הצרה בהדיא, משום דאפירקין דלעיל קאי. והא דלא קאמר "לאיתויי צרת סוטה וצרת מחזיר גרושה", משום דאילונית דמיא טפי לעריות, שמותרות למת ואסורות לייבם:
Tosafot on Yevamot 20a:9:1.english: To include the rival wife of an aylonit - Even though the Mishnah does not [explicitly] teach a rival wife, nevertheless it is included in [the phrase] "any [woman] whose prohibition is a prohibition of a forbidden relation [ervah]," which implies [one] whose prohibition comes on account of a forbidden relation, that is, the rival wife. And it did not need to mention the rival wife explicitly, because it refers back to the previous chapter. And as for why it does not say "to include the rival wife of a sotah and the rival wife of one who takes back his divorced wife," [it is] because an aylonit is more similar to forbidden relations, which are permitted to the deceased [brother] and forbidden to the yavam.
